versions.short: The bill would add the Route 66 National Historic Trail to the National Trails System, covering the historic alignments of U.S. Highway 66 that existed between 1926 and 1985 along a roughly 2,400-mile route from Chicago, Illinois, to Santa Monica, California. The Secretary of the Interior would administer the trail in a way that maintains its unique character and would consult with affected Indian Tribes before taking actions that would have substantial direct impacts on them. The United States would be barred from acquiring land outside federally managed areas without the owner's consent and from acquiring land extending more than an average of a quarter mile on either side of the trail, and the Secretary could not use eminent domain or condemnation. The bill would also state that the designation does not create a buffer zone or put the trail into the National Park System, does not block energy development or transmission, and does not create new permit requirements or change existing authority to grant easements and rights-of-way.
